one_line: Sena dynasty king of Bengal and learned patron of Brahmin scholarship in 12th‑century Gauda.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, medium-tall, dignified build with a scholar-king bearing rather than a bulky warrior.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, thoughtful gaze; medium-brown complexion; straight, slightly arched brows; sharp nose; neatly trimmed moustache with a short pointed beard; a small vertical sandalwood tilak on the forehead; default expression is composed and observant, softening into a slight knowing smile.
appearance.hair: Dark black hair drawn back into a tight, high Brahmin-style topknot (shikhā) at the crown; sides neatly combed; no loose strands; he wears a narrow gold circlet-like headband resting above the forehead tilak, with a small central red cabochon stone.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, cream-colored cotton angavastra-style upper cloth draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around the torso, paired with a deep maroon silk uttariya draped from the left shoulder across the chest and over the right forearm; his lower garment is a ankle-length dhoti of fine off-white cotton with a broad woven mustard-gold border, pleated in front and wrapped in the eastern Bengali style; around his waist is a simple yet regal cloth kamarbandh in muted gold, tied with the ends hanging slightly to the left; he has a short-sleeved, light beige cotton tunic (kurta-like) under the drapes, visible at the arms and neckline; jewellery is restrained but royal—one medium-width gold necklace with a flat pendant, a pair of small gold kundala earrings, a single gold armlet on his right upper arm with a subtle lotus motif, and a simple signet ring on his right hand; on his feet are brown leather sandals with simple straps, era-appropriate and practical; the textiles are mostly plain weaves with subtle woven borders and minimal patterning, emphasizing scholarly simplicity over ostentatious display.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord, held in his left hand, with one leaf loose and inscribed, symbolizing his works like the Danasagara and Adbhutasagara, while his right hand sometimes rests on the hilt of a sheathed straight-edged sword tucked discreetly at his waist.

ref_desc: Ballalasena is a medium-tall, late-middle-aged king with a medium-brown oval face, black hair in a high Brahmin topknot, cream angavastra and off-white dhoti with mustard-gold borders, deep maroon uttariya, simple gold jewellery, and a palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Ballalasena, the 12th-century Sena ruler of Bengal, as a dignified scholar-king: a medium-tall man in his late 40s–50s with a medium-brown oval face, calm thoughtful eyes, straight brows, a sharp nose, and a neatly trimmed moustache with a short pointed beard, marked by a small vertical sandalwood tilak on his forehead. His dark black hair is pulled into a tight Brahmin-style topknot (shikhā) high on the crown, with a narrow gold circlet headband and a small red stone centered above the tilak. Dress him in historically grounded eastern Indian clothing: a cream cotton angavastra-like upper cloth draped over both shoulders and around the torso; over this, a deep maroon silk uttariya falling from his left shoulder diagonally across the chest and hanging over his right forearm; an ankle-length off-white cotton dhoti with broad mustard-gold woven borders, pleated in front and wrapped in an eastern Bengali style; and a light beige short-sleeved cotton tunic visible at the neckline and sleeves. Add a muted gold cloth waist sash (kamarbandh) tied with ends hanging slightly left, simple brown leather sandals, and restrained royal jewellery: a medium gold necklace with a flat pendant, small gold kundala earrings, a single lotus-motif gold armlet on the right upper arm, and a plain signet ring on his right hand. In his left hand he firmly holds a tied bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts with a red cord and one visible inscribed leaf, while his right hand rests lightly near the hilt of a discreet straight-edged sheathed sword tucked at his waist; keep the overall palette cream, deep maroon, mustard gold, off-white, and brown, and ensure the design is modest, fully clothed, and consistent from head to toe for reuse across many panels.
